title: Hospital stay: what to bring and expect
what: When you are admitted to hospital for treatment or surgery. Here is what to bring and how the first day goes.
why: For treatment, tests, or surgery that cannot be done as an outpatient.
duration: depends on the treatment, from one day to several weeks
tell_doctor: If you need a special diet or help walking

prepare.title: Documents
prepare.text: Ask which tests are needed before admission and how long they stay valid.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Ask your doctor which to bring and which to stop.

prepare.title: Arrangements
prepare.text: Tell your work, and decide who will look after your home and family.

bring: Your daily medicines, in their packs
A phone, charger, mug, and spoon
steps: At the admissions desk, your documents are checked
You are examined, and sometimes blood is taken
A nurse takes you to your room
Your doctor meets you and explains the plan
A nurse explains the routine: ward rounds, procedures, meals
Then treatment goes ahead as planned
feel: The first day is often hectic
Ask the doctor questions during ward rounds. That is normal
after: Ask every day on rounds how treatment is going
You are usually told about discharge in advance
red_flags: If you suddenly feel much worse in the ward, press the call button or call a nurse right away

faq.q: Can I bring my own food?
faq.a: Usually yes, unless you are on a special diet. Ask the ward if there is a fridge.
Rules differ in every hospital. Check the visiting hours and rules.

faq.q: Should I bring my own medicines?
faq.a: Usually yes, in their packs. The doctor will say which to continue.

reminders.text: Hospital admission tomorrow. Pack your documents, test results, medicines, and things.
